reader.requirement: The minimum and maximum record sizes (fixed file attributes, II.2.1) are fixed when the OPEN OUTPUT (or optional I-O/EXTEND) creates the file and are not changed afterwards; a re-creation establishes new ones, and which attributes a later OPEN validates is the implementor's (GR8).
reader.edition-search: grep Edition|DialectBehavior|CobolVersion in FixedFileAttributes.cs, KeyedConnector.cs, SequentialConnector.cs#FixedAttributeConflict and FileConnector#OpenOnceEntered: the attribute check is edition-free
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers a fixed-length sequential re-creation only; not exercised: RECORD VARYING files, relative and indexed files opened with other sizes, EXTEND through a wider description

probes.printed: V1-W7-OVER-MAX=44 V1-W1-UNDER-MIN=44 V2-EXTEND-WIDER=00 V2-W10=00 V1-R2=04 L=06 [012345]
probes.expected: the creating description's VARYING 2 TO 6 bounds hold for its WRITEs (44); a sequential file records no sizes, so a wider description's EXTEND is not validated (GR8, implementor's set) and the creator's description reads the 10-character record truncated to 6 with 04 (VII.1.3.5 1b)

probes.printed: R2-IN-WIDER=39 R2-EXT-WIDER=39 R2-IO-WIDER=39 R1-IN-SAME=00 R2-RECREATE=00 R1-IN-AFTER-RECREATE=39 I2-IO-WIDER=39 I1-IN-SAME=00
probes.expected: relative and indexed stores record the sizes at creation: another size on INPUT/EXTEND/I-O is a file attribute conflict, 39 (GR8, VII.1.3.5 3f); OPEN OUTPUT re-creates and re-establishes them

probes.printed: F2-EXTEND-WIDER=00 F1-R1=00 AAAA F1-R2=00 BBBB F1-R3=00 CCCC
probes.expected: fixed-length sequential: no sizes on the medium, the reading description's length governs (implementor determination under GR8)

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR25  (4.3.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR25
OK  §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR8  (4.3.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR8

reader.notes: Keyed stores keep the creation sizes in their meta pages and refuse a different description with 39; sequential formats record no sizes, a documented determination (SequentialConnector#FixedAttributeConflict remarks; docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-146) that GR8 permits. A wider description EXTENDing a sequential file is a program outside GR25 that the implementor need not detect.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR25 (cite.py OK) against GR8: 'The implementor defines which of the fixed file attributes are validated during the execution of the OPEN statement' (cite.py: OK §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR8). The attack: the reader's own probe shows a wider description EXTENDing a sequential file and writing a 10-character record into a file created with a maximum of 6 (V2-W10=00), so the file's maximum did change. That change violates the program's obligation in GR25 ('must not subsequently be changed'). It is not a compiler defect, because GR8 explicitly leaves validation of record sizes to the implementor and allows it to vary by organization. The determination is documented: docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-146 says a record sequential file records no record boundaries or sizes. The keyed organizations validate the sizes with 39 (reader probe p25_keyed). No 1985-only form bears on this rule, since RECORD VARYING and RECORD CONTAINS integer TO integer take the same path. The verdict rests on reading GR25 as a constraint on the program, with detection governed by GR8.
